findings.title: OAuth helper imports decodeOAuthState from a path that does not exist
findings.body: After the move into `_utils/oauth/`, `createOAuthAppCredential` imports `decodeOAuthState` from `../oauth/decodeOAuthState`. From this file that resolves to `_utils/oauth/oauth/decodeOAuthState`, which is not a module. Every callback that creates credentials through this helper (HubSpot, Salesforce, Stripe, Zoom, Webex, MS Teams, Zoho, Tandem, and others) will fail to load or throw at runtime, so those OAuth installs cannot complete.

findings.title: Google token refresh persists the Zod result instead of the credential
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod safe-parse object `{ success, data }`, but Google Calendar assigns that whole object to `key` and writes it with `prisma.credential.update`. Previously the stored key was the parsed token object. On the next refresh (credential sync on or off) the credential row is replaced with that wrapper, so later `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and Google Calendar stops working for that user.

findings.title: Missing refresh tokens are replaced with the literal string "refresh_token"
findings.body: If the parsed body has no `refresh_token`, this function sets `data.refresh_token` to the string `"refresh_token"`. Callers then persist that value. Office 365 spreads the parsed object over the saved credential (`o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`), so a Microsoft refresh that omits `refresh_token` overwrites the real refresh token. The sync minimum schema also strips unknown fields, so a real refresh token is dropped and this dummy is written. Later refreshes send `refresh_token=refresh_token` and the integration is permanently invalidated.

findings.title: Sync token schema does not accept an expiry field
findings.body: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are literal property names from Zod's `toString()`, not a catch-all for numeric expiry. Zod object schemas also strip unknown keys. When credential sync is enabled, a normal token body such as `{ access_token, expires_in }` parses, but `expires_in`/`expiry_date` are removed before the result is saved. Integrations then treat the token as already expired or cannot compute expiry, and refresh loops or fails.

findings.title: Sync refresh returns a fetch Response that callers do not parse
findings.body: When sync is enabled this returns the raw `fetch` Response. Google reads `res.data` (axios-style) and never calls `response.json()`, so `token.access_token` is undefined. HubSpot, Zoho CRM, and Zoho Bigin expect an axios response and read `.accessToken` / `.data` / `.expiresIn` on that fetch Response. Those fields are missing, so the sync path the PR adds cannot refresh tokens and will throw or write garbage credentials.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sync sends credential id as the Cal user id
findings.body: `refreshAccessToken` passes `credentialId` (the credential row id) as the third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens`. That argument is posted as `calcomUserId`. The parent app therefore looks up the wrong user and returns another user's tokens or no tokens, and those tokens can be stored on this credential.

findings.title: Zoom refresh uses app slug zoomvideo instead of zoom
findings.body: The Zoom app id/slug used everywhere else in this change (callback `appId: "zoom"`, webhook lookup) is `zoom`, but `refreshOAuthTokens` is called with `"zoomvideo"`. A credential-sync endpoint keyed by app slug will not find the Zoom installation, so Zoom refresh fails whenever sync is enabled.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh calls prisma without importing it and ignores the new access token
findings.body: The new refresh block calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this file never imports `prisma`, so constructing a Salesforce client throws ReferenceError and Salesforce events fail. Even if prisma were imported, the `jsforce.Connection` is still created with `credentialKey.access_token` (the pre-refresh token) rather than `accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`, so the in-memory client keeps using the expired token. This refresh also always hits `https://login.salesforce.com` and does not go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so sandbox orgs and the new sync endpoint are both skipped.

findings.title: Webhook secret check is bypassed when the secret env var is unset
findings.body: The handler compares `req.headers[headerName] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset, that is `undefined !== undefined` when the header is also absent, so the check passes. `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is only a module-load snapshot of the env and is not rechecked here against the secret actually used for the comparison. An unauthenticated caller can then decrypt with an empty key fallback (`symmetricDecrypt(..., "")`) and create or overwrite a user's app credential JSON, including OAuth tokens.

findings.title: Credential upsert races and can attach tokens to the wrong row
findings.body: The handler does `findFirst` by `userId` + `appId` and then either updates that id or creates a new row. Concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app both miss and insert duplicates. `findFirst` also has no `type` or team filter and no order, so if a user already has more than one credential for that app the update can overwrite an arbitrary one and leave the credential the calendar/video adapters actually load stale or replaced with another account's tokens.
